frontier.hypothesis: The 7th callee-saved register is loop.c's marginal (savings 1) hoist of &D_800A3590 at insn 312; kill the hoist and the giv reduction that depends on its `add (reg 126)` term goes with it, taking the frame to 0x80 and freeing a seat for the rotation.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c move_movables hoists the loop-invariant symbol address into pseudo 126; the resulting giv combines with the load's giv at 319 and clears a reduction threshold the bare `mult 2 add 0` giv at 315 fails. Removing the invariant term drops the benefit back below threshold.
frontier.next_probe: Ordinary-C avenues first, in order: (a) restructure the inner `if` so pseudo 126's life shrinks or the address is reachable on fewer paths; (b) sink the whole `prim.p_static = ...` computation into the two arms of the mode `if` (the duplicated-statement family is available if the plain form does not do it); (c) anything that raises inner-loop register pressure, since savings 1 is a one-vote margin. Only once those are spent and banked does .claude/rules/defeat-licm-hoist-var-reuse.md become the relevant family, and it is FAKE-gated so it needs this exhaustion ledger to be real first.

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining 101 is a 5-seat callee-saved rotation that should be typed by the solver rather than probed by hand.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc/global-alloc seat assignment: arg0 wants $s1, var_s0 wants $s0, ctx wants $s2, var_s3 wants $s3, c60 wants $s4. Because almost every scored insn names a register, this rotation is what the 101 is made of - which is exactly why the s1 diagnostic that changed the array's index variable moved the score by 0.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver (global.c + local-alloc models) via inverse_compose.py classify on the floor-101 chassis, once with the extra H3 allocno present and once with it absent, for a typed REACHABLE/FORECLOSED verdict plus a ranked C-lever vector. If the 6-allocno case comes back FORECLOSED, do the H3 hoist work first and re-classify.

frontier.hypothesis: IconC70's real tail layout (bytes 0x8..0x20) is recoverable from func_80069898's other callers, replacing the placeholder that currently blocks submission.
frontier.mechanism: The 0x20 size is proven by frame arithmetic, but candidate.c spells the tail as `s16 sp50[12]`, which is a placeholder rather than evidence and would not survive review. func_80069898's other callers write the fields this function leaves alone, and their asm names the real offsets and widths.
frontier.next_probe: Read the $a1-relative stores in func_8006B120, func_8006CFBC, func_800720FC, func_80074488 and func_8006F97C, build the true field list, replace the placeholder, re-measure, and propagate the corrected type to func_8006F97C's ledger.
